               <ns0:p n="3">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:230" />3 And Jesus put forth <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> hand, and touched him, saying, I will, be thou clean—And immediate<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly his leprosie was cleansed.<ns0:note place="bottom">By the Law of God, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 5.3. he that touched another, who was unclean (as the <ns0:hi>Leper</ns0:hi> was, <ns0:hi>Levit. ch.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 14.) was <ns0:hi>unclean,</ns0:hi> how then doth Christ (who was subject to the Law) touch the <ns0:hi>Leper?</ns0:hi> Some say he did not touch the <ns0:hi>unclean Leper,</ns0:hi> but him that was a Leper, and by his touch made clean. But it is a better Answer, that what Christ did as he was God, (such were his miraculous Operations) he could not contract any ritual <ns0:hi>uncleanness</ns0:hi> by; and Po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sibly under the Law, the <ns0:hi>Priest</ns0:hi> was exempted from that uncleanness, for he came very near the <ns0:hi>Leper,</ns0:hi> in his Office about him expressed, <ns0:hi>Levit. ch.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 14. Nor do we read of any un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cleanness contracted by <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> in his performance of his Office to <ns0:hi>Miriam</ns0:hi> under her <ns0:hi>Leprosie,</ns0:hi> nor by the <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 26.20. tho it be said, <ns0:hi>They thrust out Vzziah.</ns0:hi> Christ by putting forth his hand, shewed his kindness to this miserable Creature: By healing him <ns0:hi>with a touch,</ns0:hi> he shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed his Divine Power, Saying, <ns0:hi>I will, be thou clean.</ns0:hi> He an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swereth him in his own term, <ns0:hi>I will,</ns0:hi> and then <ns0:hi>Commands the thing.</ns0:hi> How acceptable is Faith to God? And <ns0:hi>imme<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diately</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Leprosie</ns0:hi> was cleansed, that is, removed, the word <ns0:hi>immediately</ns0:hi> confirms the Miracle, it was not only a thing done without ordinary means, but without the ordinary time, requisite for such a Cure.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man but go thy way, shew thy self to the Priest, and offer the gift that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Levit. 14.3.4.10.</ns0:note> Moses command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, for a testimony unto them.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some think that our Saviour, only commanded him <ns0:hi>Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence until he had shewed himself unto the Priest,</ns0:hi> and he according to the Law, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 13. should have pronounced him clean, lest their Envy upon hearing of it, should have caused them to have obscured the Miracle, by delaying to pronounce him clean; but it is observable that this was not the only time when Christ commanded those upon whom he had wrought Miracles to say nothing of it, see <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 9.30. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 12.16. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.9. It is therefore more probable, that this Precept was not to be understood with that <ns0:hi>Limitation,</ns0:hi> but that Christ did it, either that he might not be thought to seek his own Glory, or rather, because Christ judged it not yet time by his Miracles to be publickly made known: But he sends him to the <ns0:hi>Priest,</ns0:hi> both to teach him <ns0:hi>Obedience to the Law,</ns0:hi> and that the <ns0:hi>Truth of the Miracle</ns0:hi> might by a pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lick Record be confirmed, he also Commands him to offer the Gift appointed by the Law, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 14. thereby both ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />knowledging his Cure to be from God, and Testifying his Thankfulness. <ns0:hi>That Moses Commanded,</ns0:hi> to shew that he came not to oppose <ns0:hi>Moses. For a Testimony unto them,</ns0:hi> that hereafter it may be a Testimony unto them, that I am more than the Son of Man, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 5.36.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 7.1.</ns0:note> And when Jesus was entred into Caper<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naum, there came unto him a centurion beseech<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And saying, Lord, my servant lyeth at home sick of the palsie and grievously tormented.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 The centurion answered, and said, Lord, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 15.19.21.</ns0:note> I am not worthy that thou should'st come under my roof, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 107.20.</ns0:note> speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 For I am a man under authority, having sol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diers under me, and I say to this <ns0:hi>man,</ns0:hi> Go, and he goeth, and to another Come, and he cometh, and to my servant Do this, and he doth it.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 When Jesus heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith no not in Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">Many think, that this story was in order before the other. It is related by <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 7.1. with some larger Circumstances, there is only <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>is Di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>erence betwixt the two Evangelists, <ns0:hi>Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ee<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s to speak, as if the <ns0:hi>Centurion</ns0:hi> at first came in Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son to him, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, that he first sent the <ns0:hi>Elders of</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to him, then some <ns0:hi>Friends.</ns0:hi> But we are accounted our selves to do that which we set others on work to do. <ns0:hi>There came unto him a Centurion,</ns0:hi> there came some Elders of the <ns0:hi>Iews first,</ns0:hi> then some particular Friends of one that was a <ns0:hi>Roman Captain,</ns0:hi> to him, to tell him that the C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ptain had a Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant at his house, that lay grievously sick of, and tormented with the Palsie. That which we usually call the dead Palsie, in which a fit of the <ns0:hi>Apoplexy</ns0:hi> usually issueth, when it doth not presently kill. Our Lord promiseth to come, and heal him, therein shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing both his kindness, and how acceptable to him, the Huma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity of this Centurion to his Servant was<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> The <ns0:hi>Centurion</ns0:hi> by his Friends, as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> tells us, sends to him, desiring him not to trouble himself to that degree, telling him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 1. That it was a favour of which he was not worthy. The best Men have always the meanest Thoughts of themselves. 2. That it was needless, for if he would only <ns0:hi>speak the word,</ns0:hi> commanding out the Distemper, that was enough to effect the Cure. For he tells him, that he believed <ns0:hi>Diseases</ns0:hi> were as much at <ns0:hi>Christ's Command,</ns0:hi> as his Servants were at his Command. That they came at Gods Command, wrought according to their Commission from God, and went off when God com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded them off; so that if he, tho at a distance, would Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand off his Servants disease, it would be as effectual as his Presence; whether this Captain were actually Proselyted to the <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>wish Religion,</ns0:hi> or no, is incertain: It should seem by our Saviour's next word, that he was not an <ns0:hi>Israelite</ns0:hi>; but it is most certain, that he had a right Notion of the <ns0:hi>Power of the true God,</ns0:hi> and it looks very probable, that he had a <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velation of Christ,</ns0:hi> as the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Son of God. W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>en Iesus heard this he marvelled.</ns0:hi> Admiration agreed not to Christ as God, but as man it did. And <ns0:hi>said to those that followed him, Verily I say unto you. I have not found so great Faith in Israel.</ns0:hi> That is, in the Generality of the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> for if we speak of particular Persons, both <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had shewed a greater Faith. This Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sion is enough to let us know, that the Centurion was no native <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> and make it probable he was not of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Church, which might be, tho he was so kind to the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Nation as to build them a Synagogue, upon which Account, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 7.3. &c. the Elders of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> pleaded with Christ for him. This made our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our go on, Prophecying of a further Conversion of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And I say you, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1.11.</ns0:note> many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham, Isaac and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 21.43.</ns0:note> the children of the Kingdom <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 13.42.50. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 22.13. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 24.51. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 25.30.</ns0:note> shall be cast out into outer darkness, there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">That is, in short, many of those who are now Heathens shall be saved: And many of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> shall be damned. Many, not all, shall come from the <ns0:hi>East</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>West,</ns0:hi> from all parts, from the remotest parts in the World. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>East, West, North,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>South, Luk.</ns0:hi> 13.29. so <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.12. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 43.5, 6. <ns0:hi>and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Iacob in the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of God,</ns0:hi> in Heaven where <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> the Heads of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Nation</ns0:hi> are, to whom the Promises were made. Or, in the <ns0:hi>Church of God,</ns0:hi> for the Church Trium<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phant, and Militant are both but one Church: They shall <ns0:hi>sit down with them,</ns0:hi> as Men sit down at a Banquet, an Expre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ssion oft used, to signifie, the Rest and Pleasure, the Saints shall have in Heaven, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 25.6, 7, 8. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 22.29, 30. But <ns0:hi>the Children of the Kingdom,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> who boast much that they are the Children of <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> and think them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves the only Church, and the only Heirs of Glory, and who are indeed the only Church of God, as yet. <ns0:hi>Shall be cast out into outer Darkness</ns0:hi>: Either, the Darkness of Errors, Ignorance, and Superstition, the Gospel-Light shall not shine upon them, they shall be no more the Church of God: Or the <ns0:hi>Darkness of Hell,</ns0:hi> where shall be nothing but Pain and Misery, and Lamentations for the Gospel, and the Grace thereof first offered to them, but unthankfully rejected by them, by which they judge themselves unworthy of the Grace of God, and of E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternal Life, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 13.46.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way, and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee and his servant was healed in the self same hour.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>And they that were sent returning to the House, found the Servant whole that had been sick,</ns0:hi> Luk. 7. v. 10. so as it seemeth, that what Christ <ns0:hi>said unto the Centu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rion,</ns0:hi> must be Interpreted to those whom the Centurion sent in his Name. Go your way, your Business is done, the <ns0:hi>Cen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turions</ns0:hi> Faith hath obtained, it shall be done to him, as he hath believed; where <ns0:hi>believing</ns0:hi> must signifie, <ns0:hi>A certain Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swasion of the Power of Christ,</ns0:hi> with a <ns0:hi>relying on his Mercy and Goodness.</ns0:hi> The proximate Object of Faith is some <ns0:hi>word of God.</ns0:hi> How far this Centurion was acquainted with the Oracles of the Old Testament (tho he lived amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and as appears by his building a Synagogue for them, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 7. had a kindness for their Religio<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>) I cannot tell. It is most probable<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that he had some immediate Revelation of God concerning Christ, which he is here said to have believed, and to have had a full perswasion of and trusted in. All Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velations of God are the Object of Faith, tho the Scriptures be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing now written, are to us that have them, the Tests, and Touch<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tones to try such impressions by. <ns0:hi>As thou believest,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>because thou believest.</ns0:hi> Our Faith is not meritorious of the least Mercies, but it is an Exercise of Grace which gives Glory to God, and receiveth the reward not of <ns0:hi>Debt</ns0:hi> but of <ns0:hi>Grace.</ns0:hi> The Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racle appeared in that the Disease was of an incurable Nature, and the Cure was wrought without Application of means, and in such a Moment of time as means, tho used, could not have wrought it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:230" />14 And when Jesus was come into Peters house, he saw his wifes mother laid, and sick of a fea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she arose and ministred unto them.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Story is related with some further Circumstances. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.29. <ns0:hi>Lu.</ns0:hi> 4.38, 39. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> tells us, it was the house of <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Andrew</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> (it seems they lived there together) that <ns0:hi>they told him of her Sickness,</ns0:hi> after he had been there some time, <ns0:hi>That he took her by the hand, and lift her up. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, it was a <ns0:hi>great Feaver that they besought him for her, That he stood over her and rebuked the Feaver.</ns0:hi> Here is no Contradiction, only some Amplificati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons of the Story. It is plain from this Text, that <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was a Married <ns0:hi>Man,</ns0:hi> and continued so, tho called to be an Apo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tle, and that he had a Family. Feavers are ordinary Distempers, and often cured by ordinary means, but this was a <ns0:hi>great Fea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver.</ns0:hi> The Miracle here was not in the Cure of an <ns0:hi>incurable Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sease,</ns0:hi> but in the way of the Cure, by a <ns0:hi>touch of his hand,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>lifting her up,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Suddenness</ns0:hi> of the Cure, it <ns0:hi>immediate<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly left her,</ns0:hi> and her <ns0:hi>sudden recovery of Strength,</ns0:hi> that she could presently arise and <ns0:hi>Minister</ns0:hi> to them; that she could do it, argued her Cure Miraculous; that she did do it, argues her sense of Christs goodness, and thankfulness, and teacheth us the use we should make of all Gods gracious Providences to us, to make us fitter for the Service of God, and to employ our selves in it; so taking the <ns0:hi>Cup of Salvation,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>praising</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Name of the Lord, Psal.</ns0:hi> 116.13.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils, and he cast out the spirits with <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> word, and healed all that were sick.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 That it might be fulfilled which was spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken by Esaias the prophet, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isaiah 53.4.</ns0:note> Himself took our infirmities, and bare <ns0:hi>our</ns0:hi> sicknesses.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.32. and <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 4.40. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> adds, he <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>aid his hands upon them,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>healed them,</ns0:hi> we before <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 4, <ns0:hi>v,</ns0:hi> 24<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> shewed who were meant by Persons <ns0:hi>possesse<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> by Devils.</ns0:hi> It is only observable that it is said, he cast out the Devils by <ns0:hi>his word,</ns0:hi> by the same power by which he made the World, and all things therein, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1. his Authoritative word: <ns0:hi>he healed all that were Sick,</ns0:hi> that is, all that were brought to him; <ns0:hi>laying on</ns0:hi> of his Hands, was but an exter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal <ns0:hi>Symbol,</ns0:hi> or rite used <ns0:hi>in blessing,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Miraculous operations,</ns0:hi> and in <ns0:hi>ordination</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Ministers.</ns0:hi> The great question is, how that which the Prophet <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> said <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 53.4. was fulfilled by these Miraculous operations. The words are, <ns0:hi>Surely he hath born our Griefs, and carried our Sorrows,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>By his Stripes we are healed</ns0:hi>; and the Apostle <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> referring to that Text saith, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.24. <ns0:hi>who bare our Sins in his Body on the Tree.</ns0:hi> The words neither seem truly quoted, nor doth the Sense appear the same, the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> applying what the Prophet seems to speak of our Sins, to our <ns0:hi>Bodily infirmi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties,</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>bearing them</ns0:hi> to his <ns0:hi>curing them,</ns0:hi> whereas <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> seemeth to apply it to his bearing our Sins, that is, the punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of our Sins, in his <ns0:hi>Stripes,</ns0:hi> and by his Sufferings on the Cross. What I observed before is here to be considered, that the <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> in their quotations out of the old Testament took themselves only concerned to keep to the Sense, not exactly to the Words (which is a liberty we ordinarily take in Quotati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons) 2. As to the <ns0:hi>Sense, Grief</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sorrows,</ns0:hi> are Terms capable of an Interpretation, as to whatsoever comes upon us, as the Fruit, and demerit of our Sins, so as the Prophet designed to express <ns0:hi>Christs</ns0:hi> Suffering all the punishment due to us for Sin, of which Nature are all the Afflictions of this Life, and Death it self, as well as the pains of Hell. The only question is, How <ns0:hi>Matthews</ns0:hi> saying, <ns0:hi>he healed</ns0:hi> the peoples Diseases, an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered the Prophets Expression, He <ns0:hi>bare our Griefs,</ns0:hi> and car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried our <ns0:hi>Sorrows.</ns0:hi> This Scripture was twice fulfilled in Christ: as to their <ns0:hi>Bodily Griefs and Sorrows,</ns0:hi> that is mentioned by <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi>; tho he bare them not all in his own Body, yet he had Compassion on Men with Reference to them, and shewed himself Afflicted in their Afflictions, by his putting forth his Divine Power to heal them, and he bare the <ns0:hi>Guilt</ns0:hi> that was the cause of these and other <ns0:hi>Griefs</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sorrows</ns0:hi> upon the Tree, as is said by <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and he therefore healed them, that he might demonstrate himself to be the true <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> Prophesied of by <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> who was to come, who was to <ns0:hi>bear our Griefs, and to carry our Sorrows.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Now when Jesus saw great multitudes a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.<ns0:note place="bottom">When Jesus did these things before mentioned, he was in <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pernaum, v.</ns0:hi> 5. but the Multitudes pre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ing him, he gave or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der to pass over theSea of Galilee, otherwise called the <ns0:hi>Sea</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Ti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berias, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>o.</ns0:hi> 6.1.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And a certain scribe came and said unto him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air <ns0:hi>have</ns0:hi> nests, but the Son of man hath not where to lay <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> head.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have the same Story, <ns0:hi>Lu.</ns0:hi> 9.57. only <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith it was <ns0:hi>as they went in the way</ns0:hi>: and saith, <ns0:hi>a certain Man</ns0:hi> thus said unto him. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> more particularly describeth the Man from his <ns0:hi>Office,</ns0:hi> or ordinary imployment. Both agree in what he said to our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Master</ns0:hi>! (so they usually called their <ns0:hi>Teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers</ns0:hi> to whose conduct they gave up themselves) <ns0:hi>I will follow thee,</ns0:hi> that is, I am resolved, or I am ready to follow thee, <ns0:hi>whi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thersoever thou goest.</ns0:hi> Thus men often take up suddain Reso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lutions, to walk with God and to be his Servants, upon Sinister Accounts, and before they have well considered what they are like to meet withal, who own themselves the Disciples of Christ. Our Saviour knowing his Heart, and that this Reso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lution was either bottomed in his Curiosity, to see his <ns0:hi>Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles,</ns0:hi> or in an hope of some livelyhood from hi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ts him with an Answer, letting him know what difficulties those that fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed him must look to meet with. <ns0:hi>The Foxes have holes, &c.</ns0:hi> Alas! thou doest not know what it is to <ns0:hi>follow me,</ns0:hi> my External Condition is worse then that of the <ns0:hi>Birds of the Air,</ns0:hi> they have fixed Ne<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ts, or the Beasts of the Earth, the worst of them have holes, but I have no fixed Habitation on Earth. He both here and in many other Texts calls himself <ns0:hi>The Son of Man</ns0:hi> (a name never, that we read of, given to him but by himself) <ns0:hi>To declare the truth of his humane Nature,</ns0:hi> and that he had a Natural Compassion for Men, that he was a Child born, a Son given to us, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 9.6. The Person Prophesied of as the <ns0:hi>Messias, Dan.</ns0:hi> 7.13. The Person mentioned, who was to <ns0:hi>have all things put under his feet, Psal.</ns0:hi> 8.6. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor</ns0:hi> 15.27. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.8.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go, and bury my father.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But Jesus said unto him, Follow me, and let the dead bury their dead.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> repeating the same <ns0:hi>History, Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.59, 60. saith, that Christ said to this Man <ns0:hi>follow me,</ns0:hi> he replyeth, Lord! Suffer <ns0:hi>me first to go and bury my Father,</ns0:hi> to live at home with my Father who is an old Man, till I have performed my last filial Office to him in burying him. Others think that he was al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ready dead, and that this Disciple would not have begged leave for so incertain a time. Christ saith unto him <ns0:hi>follow me,</ns0:hi> not that our Lord disapproved the decent manner of burying the dead, but by this let him know, <ns0:hi>that no Office of love and duty to Men, must be preferred before our duty to God,</ns0:hi> to whom we owe our first obedience. It appeareth by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.60. That this Disciple was called to Preach the Gospel, a work not to be omitted, or neglected for any Offices to men. Of old, the <ns0:hi>High Priests,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Nazarites,</ns0:hi> were not to touch <ns0:hi>dead Bodies, Numb.</ns0:hi> 6.6. because of their Separation to the more immediate Service of God, Preachers of the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel ought to keep themselves as free as they can from what may distract them, saith our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Let the dead-bury the dead.</ns0:hi> There are enough to bury the dead, Persons that are spiritually dead, not alive to God, let them take care of those meaner Offices. I have higher imployment for thee than that is. Lawful, and decent Offices become sinful, when they hin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der greater duties.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:231" />28 And when he was come to the other side, unto the countrey of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed of devils, coming out of the tombs exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass that way.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Hi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ory is related by <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.1.2, 3, 4, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and by <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.26, 27. more largely than by <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> The other two <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> report it to be done in the Country of the <ns0:hi>Ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />darenes, Matthew</ns0:hi> in the Country of the <ns0:hi>Gergesenes,</ns0:hi> they were the same People, sometimes denominated from one great Ci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty in their Territories, sometimes from another, who so read<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the Story in all 3 <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> will easily conclude it the same<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> tho related with different Circumstances. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, there was <ns0:hi>two</ns0:hi> of these <ns0:hi>Daem<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>niacks. Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> mention but one, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, the Man <ns0:hi>had Devils a long time, that he ware no Cloths, neither abode in any house but in the Tombs. Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>There met him out of the Tombs a man with an unclean Spirit, who had his dwelling amongst the Tombs, and no man could bind him, no not with Chains. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he had been often bound with Fetters, and Chains, and the Chains had been pluckt asunder by him, and the Fetters broken in pieces, neither could any man tame him, and al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ways Night and Day, he was in the Mountains, and in the Tombs crying, and cutting himself with Stones Matthew</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> came out of the <ns0:hi>Tombs,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>exceeding fierce,</ns0:hi> so as none <ns0:hi>could pass that way.</ns0:hi> Divines agree, that the Power of the Evil Angels was not abated by their <ns0:hi>fall,</ns0:hi> they were only depraved in the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r <ns0:hi>Will.</ns0:hi> That the power of an Angel is much more, thanis here mentioned, is out of question. That the Evil Angels do not exert this Power upon us is from the re<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>training Power of God, we live in the A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r in which the Devil hath a Principality, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.2. why God at that time suffered the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil more to Exercise this power over the Bodies of Men<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> we probably shewed before upon <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 4.24. the World was grown very ignorant, and wicked, and Sottishly Superstitious: besides he was now come, who was to destroy the Works of the Devil, and was to shew his Divine Power in casting him out. The Jews buried their dead out of their Cities, the rich<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er of them had <ns0:hi>Tombs hewed out of Rocks, &c.</ns0:hi> and those very large as may be learned from <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 65.4. <ns0:hi>Io.</ns0:hi> 20.6. The Devil chose these places partly to <ns0:hi>affright Persons</ns0:hi> through the horror of the places, and torment the possessed with Noy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

Lukes</ns0:hi> Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29. is much the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ame with <ns0:hi>Marks.</ns0:hi> The Devils possessing these poor Creatures, hearing Christ to whose power they knew they were subject to command them out of this Man, or these two Men, said, <ns0:hi>What have we to do with thee, Iesus thou Son of God?</ns0:hi> The Devils knew Christ to be <ns0:hi>the Son of God,</ns0:hi> tho the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would not believe it, they say un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to him, <ns0:hi>what have we to do with thee?</ns0:hi> an usual Phrase made use of, where men had no desire to be troubled with the Compa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny, Converse or I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>portunity of others, <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 22.24. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 16.20. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 9.18. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 35.21. <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 3.4. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.4. when they came to him with some ingrateful motions, <ns0:hi>&c. art thou come hither to torment us bef<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        </ns0:gap>re the time?</ns0:hi> either they look upon the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>r Dispossession as a Torment, for the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil is not at quiet, but when he is doing Evil, and as this is the Tempest of the old Serpent, so we shall observe that he Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municateth it to his Seed, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 4.16. or else the Devil was a fraid lest Christ should have commanded him to his Chains, before the day of Judgment.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="32">32 And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine, and behold, the whole herd of swine, ran violently down a steep place into the Sea, and perished in the waters.<ns0:note place="bottom">

               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> in th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s differ not from <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> only they add, that they told it in the <ns0:hi>City,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Country</ns0:hi> Those that most serve the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> are afraid of him, when he cometh to shew himself in his true Colours. These Men go, and publish abroad the Miracle, what had happened to the Man that was so famous an Object of the <ns0:hi>Devils</ns0:hi> malice, and what had happened to the Swine.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And behold the whole city came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him,<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 16.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> they besought him, that he would depart out of their coasts.<ns0:note place="bottom">Both <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> here add much. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. <ns0:hi>And they went out to see what it was that was done. And they came to Iesus, and saw him that was possessed with a Devil, and had the Legion, sit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting, and Clothed, and in his right mind, and they were afraid, And they that saw it told them how it befell to him, that was possessed with the Devil, and also concerning the Swine: And they began to pray him to depart out of their Coasts. And when he was come into the Ship, he that had been possessed by the Devil, prayed him that he might be with him. How be it Iesus suffered him not, but said unto him. Go home to thy Friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had Compassion on thee. And he departed and began to publish in Decapolis, how great things Iesus had done for him, and all men did mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vel.</ns0:hi> Luke saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.26.28, 29. <ns0:hi>Then the whole Multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude of the Country of the</ns0:hi> Gadarens, <ns0:hi>round about besought him to depart from them, for they were taken with great fear<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and he went up into the Ship, and departed back again. Now the Man out of whom the Devils were departed, besought
him that he might be with him, but Iesus sent him away, sa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ing, Return to thine own House, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee: And he went away, and pub<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ished throughout the who<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e City how great things Iesus had d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ne unto h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>m</ns0:hi>: By the <ns0:hi>whole City,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>whole Country,</ns0:hi> we must understand a very great part of them <ns0:hi>came out to meet Iesus: Mark</ns0:hi> expoundeth it, <ns0:hi>to see that which was done, and to beseech <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>im to depart out of their Coast</ns0:hi>: They <ns0:hi>saw him,</ns0:hi> and not him only, but him that had been <ns0:hi>possessed of the Devils, sitting at his Feet clothed,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>his right mind.</ns0:hi> A great Miracle wrought. They did not only see it, but they heard their Servants, the <ns0:hi>Swine-Herds arresting</ns0:hi> it, they had all the external <ns0:hi>means of Faith</ns0:hi> imaginable: How are they affected? The Text saith, <ns0:hi>they were afraid.</ns0:hi> An awe of this great <ns0:hi>Person seized them,</ns0:hi> and possibly they were afraid, le<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t he should have done them some further Evil. What is the effect of this Fear? Surely they will fall down at his Feet, beg his Grace and Favour, and that he would continue with them, and be the Author of more good amongst them. Tho they had lost two thousand Swine, yet they were delivered from the Fear of him that was possessed with the Devil. And that poor Creature was delivered from as great an Affliction as we can imagine. No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing of all this. They <ns0:hi>came</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prayed,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>besought him to go out of their Coasts</ns0:hi>: Certainly, our Saviour's knowledge of the Nature of this People, and what was in their Hearts, provoked him to give the <ns0:hi>Devils</ns0:hi> such a Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berty as he did, to destroy their <ns0:hi>Swine</ns0:hi>; we are ordinarily pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nished, in the thing wherein we offend, we need no more than our ordinary Wishes, and Prayers to ruin us: Who shall hereafter tell us of <ns0:hi>a Power in Mans Will,</ns0:hi> to do that <ns0:hi>which is spiritually good,</ns0:hi> upon a <ns0:hi>Moral Suasion,</ns0:hi> what higher <ns0:hi>Moral Suasion,</ns0:hi> could these <ns0:hi>Gadarens</ns0:hi> have had, than the sight of Christ, and what he had done, afforded, (yet for ought ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pears) they were Unanimous in this Desire, that Christ should be gone. They do not do what was in their Power to do, desiring him to stay. But oh! How dangerous a thing it is, for Men to reject Christ, he <ns0:hi>immediately departeth,</ns0:hi> and we do not read that he came here any more. But he out of whom the <ns0:hi>Devils</ns0:hi> were cast abideth with him, sits at his Feet, desires he may go along with him. How great a difference there is, betwixt <ns0:hi>seeing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hearing of Christ,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Tas<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ng</ns0:hi> how good he is. The poor <ns0:hi>demoniack,</ns0:hi> would have left his Country, and gone with him. But Christ suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fered him not, probably he saw it would be more for the Glory of God for him to stay, he therefore Commands him to <ns0:hi>return to his House, and shew what God had done for him,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>how he had Compassion on him.</ns0:hi> We cannot more shew our Thankfulness to God, than by declaring his wonderful Works, and what in particular he hath done for us. This poor Man doth accordingly, and publisheth the Name of Christ in <ns0:hi>De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />capolis,</ns0:hi> which Name comprehendeth a space of the Country, within which were ten Cities (as the word doth signifie) whereof <ns0:hi>Gadara</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Pliny</ns0:hi>) was one, from which City these People had their Denomination of <ns0:hi>Gadarenes</ns0:hi>; that is, Citizens of <ns0:hi>Gadara</ns0:hi>: Or, Inhabitants of the Country ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jacent to that City.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
